# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A; no commentary)

## BOOK 1: "Her Benny: A Story of Street Life" by Silas K. Hocking (1879 preface; illustrated by H. Tuck; publ. Frederick Warne & Co.)
Dedication: "To My Bairns (GOD BLESS THEM!)". Frontispiece: Benny and Nelly Bates in the hut of Joe Wrag (p.30). Preface: author's pastoral work in Liverpool (3 yrs); Benny, Nell, Perks, Joe Wrag, Granny, Eva Lawrence drawn from life; not all street children bad.

Chapters: I Brother and Sister; II Addler's Hall; III Roughing it; IV A Friend in Need; V "O Death! what dost thou mean?"; VI In which Benny makes a Discovery; VII Two Visits; VIII In which Joe Wrag has a Vision; IX Tempted; X In the Woods; XI Benny Prays; XII Fading away; XIII The Tide turns; XIV A Glimpse of Paradise; XV A terrible Alternative; XVI An Experiment; XVII Perks again; XVIII Adrift; XIX The Border-Land; XX Life at the Farm; XXI An Accident; XXII Recognition; XXIII The Question settled; XXIV The Reward of Well-doing.

**Characters:** Benny Bates (~11-12, sturdy, dialect speech, "By golly!", somersaults, stands on head when happy; later learns to read/write). Nelly/"Nell" Bates (9, pale, round dreamy eyes, flaxen hair, sees pictures in fire, cough; dies of decline in Infirmary, buried at public expense, New Cemetery east of town). Dick Bates (father, drunk, beats Benny with leather strap for sixpence; drowns himself at dock after dream; "Saviour of my Mary, save me!"). Stepmother Sall (coarse, drunk). First wife Mary (Benny's mother; read Bible; promised to meet in heaven). Joe Wrag (night watchman, hut near fire, Calvinist "reprobate" fear; "Purty little hangel"; has runaway son; vision of rainbow "Whosoever cometh..."; wife Mary Wrag, sour then changed; Sunday tea-meetings; Bethel). Betty Barker/"granny" (Tempest Court, Copperas Hill; husband was Joe's mate; reads St Matthew 2 at Christmas). Perks (red hair, thief, cunning; plagues Benny; later convicted, real name John Cadger alias Peeler; burglary & manslaughter, 21 yrs penal servitude; interview in cell; "wish I wur dead"). Bill Tucker (boy). Mr. Lawrence (merchant, Liverpool office; employs Benny; accuses him of theft of £5 note). Eva Lawrence (~10 yrs, gave Benny new shilling, sings "Love at Home"; later grown; Mrs. Munroe's niece). Mr. Morgan (clerk). Inspector Sharp (police). Mrs. Lawrence. Eva's singing; the lucky shilling. Mrs. Fisher (farm; son Rob died; kind); John Fisher (Scout Farm farmer); sons Harry & George (college); baby Winnie. Mr. Munroe (Brooklands; horse bolt; Benny stops it, breaks arm); Mrs. Munroe; Miss "Dot" Munroe. Giles (carter boy). Mr. Jones (night school, Scoutleigh). Constable/PC. Nurse (Infirmary; "elect are whosoever will"). Dick Somerset (Joe's tea guest). Thatcher not in book 1.

**Places:** Liverpool; Lord Street; St George's Church (trysting place, 4 o'clock); Town Hall clock; Landing-stage/Woodside ferry; Joe's fire near roads being mended; Addler's Hall & Bowker's Row (off Scotland Road, near docks); Park Lane; Tempest Court; Copperas Hill; boat under tow in George's Dock; St John's Market; Eastham Woods (Raby Mere, New Ferry, Eastham); Brownlow Hill Infirmary; Falkner Square; Edge Hill; Wavertree Park; Scout Farm (near Scoutleigh; Scoutleigh Road Station); Brooklands; Manchester.

**Key events in order:** Nell & Benny sell fusees; Benny carries bag, gets sixpence; roast potatoes at Joe's fire. Father beats Benny for sixpence; Nell shields him; they steal bread/butter, flee to Joe's; sleep under boat's tow; father's "O Death" heard. Betty takes them in (penny/night). Father drowns Christmas period (Dec); children visit old home. Chapel visits (Nell converts). Benny's temptation to steal cross-over; Perks; prayer. Nell declines, dies (~Oct/Nov of next year). Benny prays at Infirmary. Benny gets job at Lawrence office (New Year, Eva). Theft of £5 note; wrongly accused; prison; Perks cell; released; homeless; sleeps at Nelly's grave; walks to country; collapses at Scout Farm, Mrs. Fisher nurses him; sunstroke. Six years at farm; conversion; Sunday school teacher. Accident at Brooklands; Eva recognizes; note found in Directory; Benny returns to Liverpool, works for Lawrence (partner later). Perks' trial; Joe's joy; Granny dead; Tempest Court demolished; Benny teaches Sunday school; children's day trip to Eastham Woods; last: Benny partner with Lawrence, married Eva, son Ben; shows shilling to children.

## BOOK 2: "The Templeton Case" by Victor L. Whitechurch (publ. Edward J. Clode, Inc., NY; 1924 text)
Chapters: I Reginald Templeton Comes to Marsh Quay; II The Visit to the Opposite Shore; III A Terrible Discovery; IV What Canon Fittleworth Found on the "Firefly"; V Detective-Sergeant Colson Discovers Clues; VI Colson is Baffled; VII The Inquest; VIII Winnie Cotterill Pays a Visit to Frattenbury; IX The Cigar Band; X Harold Grayson is Detained; XI The Canon's Cigars; XII Fresh Evidence; XIII Isaac Moss Explains; XIV Reginald Templeton's Letter; XV Detective-Sergeant Colson's Deductions; XVI Mr. Proctor Upsets Matters; XVII New Theories; XVIII Sir James Perrivale's Story; XIX Colson Makes an Appointment; XX Colson's "Imagination"; XXI Final Solution of the Problem.

**Characters:** Tom Gale (crew/cook of schooner *Lucy*, gossip, Mariner's Arms regular). Mrs. Yates (widow, landlady of Mariner's Arms; late husband's stick). Reginald Templeton (~50s, explorer back from South Africa, Fellow RGS; murdered in cabin of yacht *Firefly*, stabbed in back with triangular dagger-like blade, ~midnight-1am Sunday, Oct). Jim Webb (crew of Firefly, from Salcombe, 31 Fore Street, works for Mr. Jefferies; finds body). Mr. Proctor (Joseph Proctor, bald egg-shaped, velveteen jacket, retired cigar merchant, owns house opposite inn; great-nephew Phil, age 15; cigar cupboard; Julier Pass photo; foreman of jury; later exposed as innocent; Mr. Merrifield corn merchant alibi—bridge, played until 1:30am). Harold Grayson (artist, ~25, lodged at Mariner's Arms; left Sunday early; father Osmond Grayson, magistrate, Marlow; shell-shock; later detained at Linderton; engaged to Winnie). Canon Charles Fittleworth (cousin of Templeton; Close, Frattenbury; wife Mrs. Fittleworth; daughter Doris; cigar box from De Garcia, Cuba; found cigar band under body; brother retired colonel). Superintendent Thomas Norton (Frattenbury). Detective-Sergeant Bob Colson (wife, "Bob"; clever, careful; "Alpine ferrule" stick; blotting-pad). Major Renshaw (Chief Constable, military). Constable Gadsden (Marsh Quay). Constable Peters. Constable Drake (Linderton). Francis Norwood (coroner, solicitor, austere, hatchet face, mutton-chop whiskers, unmarried; secretly speculating in "Virginian Reefs"; dagger hanging in hall; left-handed; the murderer). Isaac Moss (Jewish diamond dealer, 13a Hatton Garden, house Fairview, 53 Compton Avenue, Brondesbury; wife; stolen diamonds 32, one left in bag; hid at hotel "Chester"). Anthony Crosby (lawyer, Crosby & Paxton, 17b Lincoln's Inn Fields; Templeton's executor). Winnie (Winifred) Cotterill (artist, 25, illustrator; Maude Wingrave flatmate, Battersea; real name Forbes). Ezra Grice (former clerk; actually lives in South Africa; confession; met Templeton, Sir James Perrivale's camp). Sir James Perrivale (big-game hunter). Dr. Hazell (gossip, bought Virginian Reefs). Rev. Alfred Carringford (vicar). Sir Peter Birchnall. Joe Thatcher (poacher, saw Moss crossing; then motor). Tyler (London detective). Blake (tobacconist, Sunday shop, copied stick). Dean (took Norwood's cigars). Mrs. Colson. Percy Forbes (Winnie's father; embezzlement; died Princetown).

**Places:** Marsh Quay (estuary, Frattenbury 2 miles N; Mariner's Arms; quay; Frattenbury Cathedral spire); Langham; Selham (Wheatsheaf); Linderton (downs); Salcombe; Ryde; Poole; Weymouth; Plymouth; Dartmouth; Battersea Park; Fleet Street; Hatton Garden; Lincoln's Inn Fields; Frattenbury Close; South Street; Canal Basin; Town Hall; Cross.

**Key events in order:** Sat Oct, Templeton arrives Firefly, rows to Moss's house, returns to Frattenbury to dine with Canon (leaves 8:30pm); Tom Gale hears "Mr Templeton"; murder; Webb finds body Sunday 7:30am; Grayson leaves early; police; Canon finds cigar band (red and gold); Norwood coroner; blotting pad clues ("see you on Saturday"; "Ezra's ices"); stick in dinghy; Colson switches sticks at Blake's; night trap, Proctor's canoe taken; Thatcher statement; Grayson detained; Canon's cigar band swapped by juror/coroner; Winnie visits; Moss confesses; inquest adjourned; Proctor detained; alibi; Norwood arrested; suicide in cell with braces. Final: Crosby to decide telling Winnie.
